summary: The school/religion context identifies the study verb, consistent with the inherited Arabic drs comparison. Source s versus glossary z is not evidence for a new root.
The negative Infectum-wa reports study in a past school situation; ʕal marks the topic of study. It does not establish a distinct religious-education sense.
A consonant-only lookup can miss the drs/drz spelling relation, but this is a lookup limitation rather than a correction to the published entry.
Is s versus z an actual dialect distinction or a transcription convention?
Does ʕal productively introduce any study topic, or is this phrasing influenced by the school context? One attestation cannot decide.
